reason: LIMA serves a clean Strapi REST API on its OWN infra (https://li-ma.nl/strapi/api/artworks) with 3,021 video/media-art works, each carrying full metadata (title, artistName, year, length, country, description, type, stillUrl). Per-work STILL images are openly served on LIMA's own CDN (https://media.li-ma.nl/view/{id}.jpg) at 736x552 (>=600px wide), HTTP 200, no auth/watermark/login — verified 9/10 samples; the legacy minority at 120x90 are width-gated out at >=600px. These are REAL per-work stills, NOT streaming-only previews, so the gating concern (preview/copyright/too-small/aggregator-only) does NOT apply. artworkUrl/artistUrl point off-site to mediakunst.net but are never needed — the still + metadata come straight from LIMA's own Strapi + media CDN. Image pipeline (still->sharp webp->R2) verified end-to-end with a real upload. CAVEAT: the Strapi metadata API is behind a WAF that throttles rapid clients to HTTP 403/500; a single organic browser load returns 200 + full data, and a ~180s quiet rest recovered it earlier, but cumulative probing today escalated the limiter to a sustained IP block that did NOT lift across ~25 min of cooldown attempts, so a clean --probe metadata pass could not complete in this session (matches the RETRY/rate-limited hint). The scraper paginates politely through a real browser (Playwright + system Chrome, exact frontend query signature) with quiet-rest backoff; full run needs a rested/fresh IP. The media image CDN itself is NOT rate-limited (stayed reachable throughout).
easy_source_found: No public opendata/bulk dump/IIIF/Solr/Navigart. The current li-ma.nl is a Gatsby SPA backed by a Strapi REST API on the museum's OWN origin: https://li-ma.nl/strapi/api/artworks?filters[titleOrder][$startsWith]=&sort=random:asc&randomSort=true&pagination[page]=N&pagination[pageSize]=20 -> {data:[{id, attributes:{title,type,year,length,description,country,artistName,artistNameOrder,titleOrder,stillUrl,artworkUrl,keywords}}], meta:{pagination:{total:3021,pageCount:152}}}. Stills on own CDN media.li-ma.nl/view/{id}.jpg (~736px). Marketing pages use Strapi build-time GraphQL (static). The old /lima/catalogue/work/list REST endpoint was retired (now SPA-fallback HTML). mediakunst.net is the shared Dutch-collections aggregator (LIMA + Stedelijk + Van Abbe + RCE) — FORBIDDEN as a source and not used.
probe_summary: Scraper written + syntax-clean; ran --probe end-to-end (harvest -> still -> R2 -> JSON write all function). Image half VERIFIED: real still 736x552 -> >=600 gate PASS -> sharp webp 29.5KB -> R2 PutObject OK -> public HEAD 200. Metadata half returned 0 rows because the Strapi WAF blocked this IP (500 on every page) after the day's cumulative probing, even through 6 in-script quiet-rest backoffs (45+75+120+150+180+200s = ~13 min) plus ~10 min external cooldowns. NOTE: before the block hardened, a single organic load DID return 200 with the full 3,021-total payload and working stillUrls — that earlier successful capture is the basis for the viable verdict and the field/count facts. Re-run --probe from a rested or different IP to get a green pass; the polite pacing + backoff are already built in.

exhibitions_entry.name: LIMA
exhibitions_entry.description: LIMA (Living Media Art), based in Amsterdam, is the largest media-art platform in the Netherlands and the successor to the Netherlands Media Art Institute / Montevideo. It preserves, distributes and presents an online catalogue of more than 3,000 single-channel video, installation and net-art works by over 500 artists — from 1960s video pioneers (Nan Hoover, Gerry Schum, Joan Jonas) to contemporary names like Seth Price, Samira Elagoz and Johan Rijpma — each documented with an openly served still frame.
exhibitions_entry.description_ko: 리마(LIMA)는 암스테르담에 자리한 네덜란드 최대의 미디어아트 플랫폼으로, 옛 네덜란드미디어아트인스티튜트(몬테비데오)의 후신이다. 1960년대 비디오 선구자부터 동시대 작가까지 500명이 넘는 작가의 싱글채널 비디오·설치·넷아트 3,000여 점을 온라인 카탈로그로 보존·배급한다. 작품마다 정지화면 스틸이 공개되어 있어, 무빙이미지 컬렉션을 시각적으로 둘러볼 수 있다.

notes: Schema fit: type ('video' mostly, plus 'installation'/'channel') -> category 'video' for all (guide §1: video = moving image). medium synthesized as 'single-channel video, {length}'; dimensions = length (HH:MM:SS); country present on ~30% of records; description present on most. ids prefixed 'li-ma-'; R2 key artworks/li-ma-collection/{id}-{hash8}-imageUrl.webp. Width gate >=600px drops the few legacy 120x90 thumbs (est ~70 of 3,021 -> est_full_count ~2,950). Scraper uses randomSort pagination accumulating UNIQUE ids until total(3021) or 25-page stall, because randomSort returns overlapping pages. OPERATIONAL: run scrape-li-ma.mjs --full from a fresh/rested IP (ideally after >30 min of no LIMA traffic) so the WAF limiter is clear; the script's quiet-rest backoff handles intermittent 403/500 but cannot beat a sustained same-IP block. mediakunst.net aggregator deliberately NOT used (FORBIDDEN). lat/lng = LIMA premises at Arie Biemondstraat 105, Amsterdam-West.
